title: Multi-zone affinity policy with graceful degradation and data-locality contract
creator: Jordan Kim
description:
Goal: Implement a multi-zone affinity policy that enforces soft data-locality guarantees for Dedicated fleets, enables staged graceful degradation during zone loss, and integrates with autoscaling and throughput reservation logic. This ticket defines policy, implementation API, control-plane checks, telemetry, and rollout plan.

Motivation:
- Customers on Dedicated want stronger locality guarantees (e.g., requests remain in-region or in-preferred-zones) without sacrificing reliable throughput during transient zone issues.
- We must enforce data residency constraints while preserving SLA-backed throughput guarantees where customers purchased regional capacity.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Control-plane policy objects: affinity_profile (preferred_zones, avoid_zones, weight_map), soft_degradation_window (seconds), residency_contract (region_id, allowed_cross_zone_seconds).
2) Scheduler: zone-weighted placement respecting affinity_profile and throughput reservations; when zone capacity is unhealthy, gradually bleed traffic using soft_degradation_window and escalate to staged failover.
3) Autoscaler integration: scale decision hooks must consider affinity weight and reservation headroom; prewarm tokens into target zones when predicted spillover > 30% of reserved throughput.
4) Router/runtime fallbacks: implement per-request routing hints (zone_preference header) and KV-cache sanity to avoid cache explosion during spillback.
5) Observability & SLOs: dashboards and alerts for p95 latency, error-rate, reservation_fulfillment, and cross-zone_egress_bytes.
6) Policy validation: control-plane prevents creation of affinity_profile that violates customer's residency_contract or signed legal constraints.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy schema (OpenAPI) merged + migrations validated in staging.
- Scheduler places 95% of requests into preferred_zones under normal load in local integration tests.
- During simulated single-zone outage, traffic is drained across other zones over soft_degradation_window with no sudden >2x spike in p95 latency.
- Throughput reservations honored across zone spillover for committed customers (reservation_fulfillment >= 99% over 24h load test).
- Data locality contract enforced: cross-zone egress > allowed_cross_zone_seconds triggers audit log and blocks new capacity allocations when contract breached.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Soft vs hard residency: choose soft_degradation_window to prioritize availability; legal residency violations must be hard-blocked at allocation time.
- Eviction policy: prefer staged soft-drain (multi-minute windows) to avoid cache blowups and client retries. This increases short-term cross-zone egress but preserves customer availability.
- Autoscale prewarm cost: prewarming increases short-term cost; threshold tuned at 30% predicted spill to reduce wasted prewarm while minimizing latency spikes.

Implementation notes & API sketches:
- New API endpoints: POST /dedicated/fleets/{id}/affinity_profiles  (body: affinity_profile JSON)
- Affinity_profile example: {"preferred_zones":["us-west1-a","us-west1-b"], "weight_map":{"us-west1-a":0.6,"us-west1-b":0.4}, "soft_degradation_window":300 }
- Residency_contract is validated against customer.billing_profile.residency_flags and account_entitlements.
- Scheduler will expose a metrics tag placement_zone and spillover_reason for telemetry.

Safety, rollout and testing:
- Stage 1: feature-flagged control-plane schema + dry-run scheduler in staging; no changes to production routing. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Multi-Zone+Affinity+Design (private).
- Stage 2: limited canary to 3 internal tenants with synthetic load and chaos injection (single-zone fail, network partition).
- Stage 3: opt-in beta for low-risk customers (non-regulated), collect 2 weeks of telemetry.
- Stage 4: GA with enforcement for customers who purchased regional residency; customers with strict legal contracts require manual approval.

Monitoring and runbooks:
- Create dashboard: fleet.affinity.placement (p90/p95 latency by placement_zone, reservation_fulfillment, cross_zone_egress_bytes).
- Alerts: reservation_fulfillment < 98% for 15m, cross_zone_egress_bytes > contract_threshold for 10m, spillover_rate > 5% sustained for 30m.
- Runbook: runbooks/dedicated/multi-zone-evacuation.md (stub created) and incident playbook for rollback and emergency regional drain.

Security/compliance:
- Any policy that would cause data to leave a sovereign region is rejected at creation time. Record audit entries to KMS-backed audit log and expose for compliance export.

Implementation plan & milestones:
- Week 1-2: Schema, control-plane validation, unit tests.
- Week 3-4: Scheduler prototype, integration tests with autoscaler hook.
- Week 5: Chaos tests (single-zone failure) and load tests for throughput reservations.
- Week 6: Canary and iter feedback, docs and runbooks.

Dependencies:
- ENG-688888 (autoscaler: prewarm hooks and prediction API)
- ENG-679332 (reservation-accounting: per-zone reservation monitoring)

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay particular attention to the eviction window length and prewarm threshold; these materially affect cost vs latency.
- Validate that the residency_contract schema maps to legal terms in Contracts team repository (contract IDs will be added to policy metadata).

release_notes_draft: Adds affinity_profile support for Dedicated fleets with staged degradation semantics. Introduces residency_contract enforcement to prevent unauthorized cross-region egress. Beta rollout followed by GA in dedicated-2025.12. Admins should review new affinity controls in Console and update SLO dashboards.
